design:
Child epic of the integrated petrochemical and polymer platform (bn op-9941 / see #77 programme).

**Fidelity target: Engineering model**

Reusable chemistry and unit operations for the major ethylene derivatives.
**Create separate sub-issues per chain with shared infrastructure
dependencies — do not implement all chains at once.**

- **Polyethylene** — ethylene -> PE
- **EO / EG** — ethylene -> ethylene oxide -> ethylene glycol
- **Ethylbenzene / styrene** — ethylene + benzene -> EB -> styrene -> PS
- **EDC / VCM / PVC** — ethylene -> EDC -> VCM -> PVC

## Cross-links worth noting now

- Ethylbenzene consumes **benzene**, so this chain couples to the BTX train,
  not only to the cracker.
- **EDC/VCM introduces chlorine.** Cl becomes a conserved element the moment
  this chain exists, and the conservation report must carry it. This is the
  only place Cl enters the complex.
- Ethylene glycol feeds **PET** alongside PTA, coupling C2 to the aromatics
  side.


## Programme constraints

No monolithic plant solvers. Reuse existing reaction/thermo/separation infrastructure. Conservation preserved across every representation change. Do not push to `main`.
title: Petchem: Ethylene derivative chains

description:
Parent: op-mzvp.2.12 (ring-RPT +4004 pcm vs OpenMC).

HYPOTHESIS UNDER TEST. Every oracle in this crate is an ENERGY-domain oracle --
sigma(E), <E'>/E, xi, the resonance integral, area conservation, p_esc, the
thermal fixed point. None of them constrains the scattering ANGLE. The only
assertion on a thermal mu in the whole crate was `(-1.0..=1.0).contains(&mu)`.
The angle sets sigma_tr = sigma_s(1 - mubar), hence the diffusion coefficient,
hence the thermal flux shape in a heterogeneous cell -- which matches the
benchmark pattern (thermal AND spatially heterogeneous fails; thermal-homogeneous
and fast-heterogeneous both pass).

THE ORACLE, in two independent halves, both from the same graphite THERMR tape
(tsl-crystalline-graphite MAT 30, 600 K, a tabulated temperature):
 - inelastic: THERMR MF=6/MT=229 carries, per incident energy, NEP groups of
   NA+2 = 18 numbers (E', f(E'), mu_1..mu_16) whose 16 cosines are EQUALLY
   PROBABLE in the lab frame. graphite_kernel_vs_njoy_thermr parses these same
   records and throws the cosines away; the new program keeps them.
 - coherent elastic: needs no MF=6 at all. E*sigma_coh(E) from MF=3/MT=230 is a
   staircase whose 296 risers ARE the Bragg edges (E_i, f_i); each scatters at
   exactly mu_i = 1 - 2 E_i / E. So mubar_el is recovered from NJOY's own cross
   section without ever reading this crate's edge table.

RESULT (2026-09-12, 400k samples/energy, 13 energies 1 meV - 3.75 eV):
worst +0.0085 absolute on mubar_inelastic at 0.0253 eV (a real 5 sigma
deviation, not noise), worst +0.0030 on mubar_coherent-elastic at 0.2 eV,
worst +0.0050 on the cross-section-weighted total.

VERDICT: EXCLUDED. mubar_total is ~0.05 over the whole thermal range, so an
error of 0.005 moves sigma_tr = sigma_s(1 - mubar) by 0.05 %. Against +4004 pcm
that is an exclusion, not a candidate.

COMMITTED AS: vv::njoy_golden::GRAPHITE_MUBAR (+ _TOL, _ELASTIC_TOL),
examples/graphite_mubar_vs_njoy_thermr.rs (golden gate + live-tape re-measure),
tests/thermal_laws_vs_njoy_thermr.rs::graphite_sab_mean_cosine_against_njoy_thermr.
title: outram-mc: thermal scattering ANGLE vs NJOY THERMR -- the leading ring-RPT hypothesis, measured and EXCLUDED

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: Follow-up from op-u6s.8 (collision now on GPU, but NO crossover vs 12-core CpuMultiThread on RTX 3050: ~1.9x slower at 1e6, gap narrowing with batch size). To actually beat multi-thread: (1) sort/compact live neutrons by reaction to cut warp divergence; (2) bank fission daughters on the GPU too (remove the per-generation CPU pass); (3) overlap event dispatches / persistent-thread kernel to shorten the sequential per-event dispatch chain; (4) test on larger batches / stronger GPU / fewer-core CPU where the measured trend predicts crossover. See crates/outram-mc-libs/docs/gpu_collision_dev_log.md for the before/after tables.

title: outram-mc: push GPU event transport past CpuMultiThread (sort-by-reaction, fused daughter banking, larger batches)
